stem: A client is diagnosed with a condition that is reportable in the nurse's jurisdiction. What is the most accurate nursing action?

options.A: Post the diagnosis publicly so community members can be warned.
options.B: Assume the bedside nurse is always the legally designated reporter in every state.
options.C: Do not report any communicable disease unless the client gives written permission.
options.D: Ensure the case is reported to the appropriate public-health department according to applicable state, local, or territorial law and facility procedure.

rationale: CDC explains that reportable conditions are reported through state, local, and territorial public-health systems and that legal reporting requirements vary by jurisdiction. The nurse should therefore follow the applicable law and institutional process rather than assume one universal reporter role.
educational_objective: Follow jurisdiction-specific public-health reporting requirements for reportable conditions.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS) — Case Surveillance
source_locator: What is Case Surveillance? / How We Conduct Case Surveillance: reporting operates under state/local/territorial laws and procedures
source_claim_supported: Reportable-condition reporting is governed by jurisdiction-specific requirements and transmitted to appropriate public-health authorities.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — public-health reporting
correction_summary: Removed the unsupported universal assumption that the bedside nurse is always the legal reporter and made the action jurisdiction-specific.
